title: John of Kanty (23 December)
hook: a Kraków professor who gave away his coat and shoes

segments.voice: Yesterday, Lucy, the martyr of Syracuse and the crown of candles. Your line was light in december.

A professor walks home through a winter street in Kraków, wearing the long gown of a university teacher. It sweeps the ground as he goes. If you lifted the hem, the story says, you would find his feet bare in the cold. Earlier, on the way, he met a poor man with nothing on his feet, and handed over his own shoes. The gown is long enough that nobody notices. A man who lectured on God all day, walking home on cold stone. This is John of Kanty.
screen: `A PROFESSOR IN A LONG GOWN.` → `BARE FEET UNDER THE HEM.` → `A LECTURER ON COLD STONE.`

segments.voice: John of Kanty was a priest who taught at the university in Kraków. His job was ideas: lectures, books, students, arguments about God. But the stories people kept about him are about clothes, food and money leaving his hands. Tradition says he gave his coat to a man shivering in the street, and on another day his shoes. When a hungry person came to the door during a meal, he was known to send his own plate out. There's a story about robbers, too. Thieves stopped him on the road, took what he had, and asked if there was anything more. He said no. Then he found a few coins sewn into his clothes, and he ran after the robbers to hand them over, because he had told them there was nothing left. They were so shaken, the story goes, that they gave everything back. Behind all this is a plain line from Luke's gospel. The crowds ask John the Baptist what they should do, and he answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none." No theory. Just coats. And in the parable of the last judgment, Jesus lists what the blessed did for him without knowing it; one line is: "Naked, and you covered me." A professor could have lectured on those verses. The stories remember him doing them, in the snow, with cold feet under his gown. His feast falls on 23 December, two days before Christmas, when the coats come out of the closet.
screen: `A PROFESSOR WHOSE JOB WAS IDEAS.` · `HIS COAT, HIS SHOES, HIS PLATE.` · `HE RAN AFTER THE ROBBERS.` · `TWO COATS: GIVE ONE AWAY.` · then, large: `NAKED, AND YOU COVERED ME.`

segments.voice: Walk slowly, in your mind, through your closet or the hooks by your door: is there a coat, a sweater, a pair of boots, a warm hat you haven't worn in a long time? Choose one, picture who might be cold without it this winter, and where it could go: a shelter, a coat drive, a parish collection, a neighbor. If you pray, offer it to God before it goes.
Kanty. The Kraków professor whose learning was real, but who is remembered for the coat and shoes he gave away, even in the snow.
Your line: the professor's coat. He lectured on God all day, and walked home barefoot. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Saint John of Kanty is remembered on 23 December, especially in Poland and at the university in Kraków where he taught; some parishes and schools collect coats and warm clothing around his feast.
